title: Baricitinib Prophylaxis for IEC-Associated Toxicities in Patients With Multiple Myeloma Receiving Commercial Cilta-Cel
official: Baricitinib as Prophylaxis for Immune Effector Cell-Associated Toxicities in Patients Receiving Commercial Cilta-Cel for Multiple Myeloma
summary:
The purpose of this research study is to see if baricitinib can reduce the side effects in people receiving ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel; CARVYKTI) treatment for multiple myeloma.

Participants will:

* Take baricitinib beginning one day before their cilta-cel infusion and continue for 28 days after the infusion
* Complete an oral drug diary entry for each dose taken of baricitinib
* Have blood, and potentially CSF, collected for research
* Be in long-term follow-up where research staff will review medical records every 6 months to check items like blood test results and side effects the participant may experience.

Participants will be in the study for approximately 4 years.
conditions: Immune Effector Cell Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Ability to understand and willingness to sign an IRB-approved informed consent
2. Age ≥ 18 years old at the time of enrollment
3. Performance Status (PS) of ≤ 2 at the time of enrollment (ECOG and/or KPS)
4. Confirmed diagnosis of relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma
5. Intending to receive commercial cilta-cel CAR T-cell therapy
6. Willing and able to comply with clinic visits and study-related procedures
7. Demonstrate adequate organ function as defined in the table below; all screening labs to be obtained as per Study Calendar. The most recent labs prior to enrollment will be used to evaluate eligibility if labs drawn more than once during screening.
8. Adequate cardiac function, as defined by the following:

   1. Absence of New York Heart Association class III or IV congestive heart failure
   2. Absence of uncontrolled angina
   3. Absence of myocardial infarction in the past 6 months
   4. Absence of clinically significant bradycardia, or another uncontrolled cardiac arrhythmia, defined as grade 3 or 4 according to the NCI-CTCAE, version 6.0
   5. Adequate cardiac function as defined by ≥ 45% Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction (LVEF) by SOC ECHO or MUGA within 180 days prior to enrollment
9. Individuals of childbearing potential (ICBP) must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 28 days prior to enrollment. NOTE: Individuals who may become pregnant are considered to have childbearing potential unless they are surgically sterile (have undergone a hysterectomy, bilateral tubal ligation, or bilateral oophorectomy) or are postmenopausal (at least 12 consecutive months with no menses without an alternative medical cause).
10. ICBP must be willing to use a highly effective contraceptive method (i.e., achieves a failure rate of \<1% per year when used consistently and correctly) from the time of informed consent until 90 days after study treatment discontinuation
11. Individuals who are having sexual relationships in which their partners may become pregnant must be willing to use condoms from the time of informed consent until 90 days after study treatment discontinuation. For a non-pregnant ICBP partner, contraception recommendations should also be considered.
12. Ability to ingest oral medications

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients who are receiving cilta-cel outside of the United States Package Insert parameters/guidelines for the initial 15 patient safety run-in portion of the study.
2. Uncontrolled intercurrent illness, including but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situations that would limit compliance with study requirements, in the opinion of the treating clinician.
3. Treatment with any investigational drug within 30 days prior to day 1 of treatment.
4. Patients with CNS myeloma involvement orunderlying neurological disorders, such as a history of Parkinson's disease or other neurodegenerative disorders.
5. History of allergic reactions attributed to compounds of similar chemical or biologic composition to baricitinib.
6. Patients with immunoglobulin light chain amyloidosis
7. Patients with active plasma cell leukemia defined as ≥ 5% circulating plasma cells at the time of starting lymphodepletion chemotherapy
8. Uncontrolled infection with tuberculosis (latent TB must be treated prior to enrollment) immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), or hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection; or other uncontrolled infection (these tests would not be required to be performed per protocol, as testing would be standard of care for pre-CAR T evaluation):

   * Participants with controlled HIV infection (undetectable viral load and CD4 count \> 200 cells/microliter) are permitted.
   * Participants with hepatitis B who have controlled infection (serum HBV DNA PCR below the limit of normal detection and receiving antiviral therapy for hepatitis B treatment/prevention against reactivation) are permitted.
   * Participants who are HCV antibody-positive with controlled infection (undetectable HCV RNA by PCR) are permitted.
9. Vaccination within 28 days prior to the first study drug administration with a vector that has replicative potential (live vaccines).
10. Patients who are unable to stop all other JAK inhibitors (baricitinib should be the only JAK inhibitor being used while on study), biologic disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), potent immunosuppressants such as azathioprine and cyclosporine, and strong OAT3 inhibitors probenecid, diclofenac, and indomethacin
